clue.text: Full-back beaten by the ball made to look bad

indicators.note: back tells us to read the synonym for full from right to left

parts.note: fed, as in well fed, means full
in tennis a player who cannot touch a serve has been aced

explanation.surface: A defender in football is humiliated when a shot whizzes past him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Full-back' looks like a football position, but it is two jobs: a synonym for full, then 'back' to turn it.
explanation.definitionFit: To deface something is to spoil its appearance, so defaced is a synonym for disfigured or marred.

clue.text: Pair of females get wet

parts.note: a dam is a mother animal, especially a horse
a pen is a female swan

explanation.surface: Two women end up soaked.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are female animals: dam (mother of livestock) and pen (female swan).
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen is to moisten, making something slightly wet.

clue.text: Defensible position Intelligence pitched between two heights without delay

parts.note: a fort is a fortified position

indicators.note: pitched between places one word between two letters

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for height, so two give two H
wit means intelligence

explanation.surface: A military camp with intelligence staff is set up between two hills at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Forthwith means immediately, at once, with no pause.

clue.text: Appeal without end, one intended to deceive tail-ender

indicators.note: without end says the synonym loses its final letter

parts.note: charm means appeal or attractiveness
a lie is a statement meant to deceive

explanation.surface: A cricketer's appeal peters out, as one meant to fool the last batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: A tail-ender bats at the bottom of a cricket order and is usually useless with the bat; a Charlie is British slang for a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A Charlie is a British slang name for a fool or incompetent, which a hopeless batsman often looks.

clue.text: Mathematician's sad secret decoded

indicators.note: decoded suggests the letters are unscrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: A mathematician's gloomy hidden truth is finally cracked.
explanation.definitionFit: René Descartes was the French philosopher who invented Cartesian coordinates, a landmark of geometry.

clue.text: Bishop's attire? Possibly

parts.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A question about what a bishop might wear, answered with a cautious maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: B plus a rearrangement of ATTIRE, and the hat is indeed clerical garb.
explanation.definitionFit: A biretta is the square cap worn by Roman Catholic clergy, including bishops, so it is part of their dress.

clue.text: Part of kit engineers have to feel confident about

indicators.note: about means the confident word goes round the other

parts.note: to bet on something is to be confident of it
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Engineers need to be sure of their equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A beret is a soft round cap worn as part of military uniform.

clue.text: Acknowledgment about chair for speaker

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: for speaker says the word is as heard when spoken

parts.note: a seat is a chair

explanation.surface: The Speaker in Parliament acknowledges a matter concerning the chair.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written note confirming that goods or money have been received.

clue.text: Fourth class neatly presented?

parts.note: type means class or kind
D is the fourth letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A fourth-class letter, tidily laid out.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that typing is just one way of presenting text neatly.
explanation.definitionFit: Typed text is set out clearly by machine rather than handwritten.

clue.text: Promptness with which a poem receives review

indicators.note: receives puts one word inside the other

parts.note: a lay is a ballad or narrative poem
a crit is informal for a critique or review

explanation.surface: A poem gets a swift critical reception.
explanation.definitionFit: Alacrity means brisk eagerness and readiness, a near synonym for speed of response.

clue.text: Duck scold, flipped into one river briefly, then another

indicators.note: then says the next river follows straight after in order
into says the turned word goes inside the shortened river
briefly means the river name loses its last letter

parts.note: the Mersey is the river at Liverpool

indicators.note: flipped means the synonym for scold is turned over

parts.note: to nag is to scold
another river, abbreviated to R as on maps

explanation.surface: A duck is told off and tossed into one river, then into a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipped' makes GAN from NAG; 'briefly' trims MERSEY to MERSE, and GAN goes 'into' it.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating diving duck with a serrated bill, so it is an example of a duck.

clue.text: Drink caught up with Dad

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
pa is an informal word for dad

explanation.surface: Someone catches up with their father over a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea, a very common drink.

clue.text: Woman heading away from chapel

indicators.note: heading away says the first letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a Bethel is a nonconformist chapel

explanation.surface: A woman walks off from the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: BETHEL is a name used for Methodist and Baptist chapels; losing its head B leaves the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a female given name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Anti-trade winds that once parted people from their land

definitions.text: that once parted people from their land

indicators.note: winds, read as twists, signals the letters are turned about

explanation.surface: Weather opposed to the trade winds that once drove settlers off their land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds' looks like the noun after 'Anti-trade', but it is the verb to twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Attainder was the old legal forfeiture of land and civil rights by someone sentenced for treason or felony.

clue.text: Crime that one's papers may confirm — one paper in particular

parts.note: identity papers prove who a person is
The FT, the Financial Times, is a particular newspaper

explanation.surface: A crime that your documents might prove, reported by a specific newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: THE FT is the Financial Times, a London daily.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing someone's personal details to impersonate them is a recognised fraud offence.

clue.text: What schoolmaster does, not one to change

indicators.note: not says a letter is left out

parts.note: a teacher trains a form, a school class
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A teacher's task is said not to be about changing anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class.
explanation.definitionFit: To transform is to alter completely, a strong synonym for change.

clue.text: I wondered idly what may be on tonight

indicators.note: idly suggests a lazy rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone muses about what's on television this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'what may be on tonight' sounds like TV listings, but it is the bed covering.
explanation.definitionFit: An eiderdown is a quilt spread on a bed, so it will be on the bed at night.

clue.text: Sort of meal for escapee?

definitions.meaning: food served to passengers aboard an aeroplane
a fugitive is running away, on the run

explanation.surface: A prisoner on the run wonders what to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes airline catering and also someone who is fleeing.

clue.text: Free-for-all in absence of security in cargo areas?

definitions.meaning: a contest with no rules or restrictions

definitions.text: in absence of security in cargo areas?
definitions.meaning: with no ship's holds locked shut by bars

explanation.surface: A brawl breaks out when a ship's cargo holds are left unsecured.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase literally: no holds (cargo areas) barred (secured).
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from wrestling, where any grip is permitted, hence an unrestrained contest.

clue.text: Check in one enticing dog

indicators.note: in puts the short check inside the other word

parts.note: a lurer is someone who entices
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

explanation.surface: Someone luring a dog checks it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a crossbred hunting dog, often greyhound with collie or terrier.

clue.text: A diamond dropped from hand at first in compound — that's insoluble

definitions.text: A diamond dropped from hand at first
definitions.meaning: in bridge, opening play with a card of a red suit from one's hand
an orange-red oxide of lead that does not dissolve in water

explanation.surface: A card player opens with a diamond in a game that can't be solved.
explanation.walkthrough: Diamonds are a red suit, and the first card played is the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Red lead is lead tetroxide, a pigment used in rust-proof paint and insoluble in water.

clue.text: Heads off from the glen with a dreamy girl

indicators.note: heads off says the first letters of the two words are dropped

explanation.surface: A dreamy girl wanders out of the valley.
explanation.walkthrough: The girl is in a dream: Helena is a heroine of Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Helena is one of the four young lovers in Shakespeare's Dream, so she is a girl from that play.

clue.text: Leaving ceremony is boring, girl admits

indicators.note: admits means the girl takes the other word inside her

parts.note: a lass is a girl
trite means stale and boring

explanation.surface: A girl confesses that a farewell ceremony was tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaving' means departing this life, not a school leavers' do.
explanation.definitionFit: The last rites are the sacraments given to a dying person, a ritual for one departing life.

clue.text: Tinned meat suppressing son's hiccup

indicators.note: suppressing means holding another letter inside

parts.note: Spam is a brand of tinned pork
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Canned meat stops a boy's hiccups.
explanation.definitionFit: A spasm is an involuntary contraction, and a hiccup is one of the diaphragm.

clue.text: Drier, so closed source of water — one litre left!

parts.note: a door pushed to is closed

indicators.note: one litre left means only one of the two L letters remains

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A well has been shut, leaving only one litre to dry out with.
explanation.walkthrough: TO is in the sense 'pull the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is used to dry oneself, so it is something that dries.

clue.text: Good to be seen in serious part of funeral, perhaps

indicators.note: to be seen in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: dire means serious or dreadful

explanation.surface: It looks good to appear solemn at a funeral.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song or lament, often sung at a burial service.

clue.text: Tweeted about hard grind

indicators.note: about here means turned round

parts.note: a bird that tweeted sang
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone posted on social media about the daily slog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tweeted' suggests social media; it is just a bird singing.
explanation.definitionFit: To gnash is to grind one's teeth together, so the two verbs share a sense.

clue.text: Complete or just a bit, it's good for you

parts.note: whole means complete
some means a certain amount, a bit

explanation.surface: Whether you eat all of it or a little, this food is healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesome describes food or activity that promotes health, beneficial to the body.

clue.text: Sides of glass put in the wrong way round in prisoner transport

indicators.note: sides here are the left and right, the two letters for those directions

indicators.text: put in the wrong way round
indicators.note: put in the wrong way round means those two letters swap places

parts.note: a tumbler is a drinking glass

explanation.surface: Bits of glass are fitted back to front in a prison van.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sides' are L and R (left and right); swapping them in TUMBLER gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel was the cart that carried condemned prisoners to the guillotine in revolutionary France.

clue.text: Mary is crazy, old Ann is backward

parts.note: mad means crazy

indicators.note: backward says the name is read in reverse

explanation.surface: Mary is mad, and old Ann is slow on the uptake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' looks like slow-witted Ann but signals reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Madonna is a title of the Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus.
